data.title: European TTF Natural Gas Rebounds on Cold Weather Outlook and Low Inventories
data.description: According to Jin10, European natural gas prices rebounded in early trading after falling in the previous session. Benchmark Dutch TTF natural gas futures rose 3.7% today to 83.80 euros per megawatt-hour. Analysts at Australia and New Zealand Banking Group said recent price declines were mainly driven by increased U.S. liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports and weaker demand from some major Asian importers, allowing more LNG cargoes to be redirected to Europe. Weather forecasts show temperatures are expected to fall, which could increase heating demand and put more pressure on gas supplies. Meanwhile, European gas storage remains relatively low, with inventories 69.9% full, compared with about 81.9% at the same time last year. This leaves the European gas market more vulnerable to supply tightness as winter demand rises.

data.title: 1inch Team Investment Fund Transfers 8,978 ETH, Reports $8.88 Million Unrealized Loss
data.description: The 1inch team investment fund transferred 8,978 ETH to a multisignature address beginning 0x9ee after remaining dormant for a year; the purpose of the transfer is unknown. According to Foresight News, citing monitoring by @ai_9684xtpa, the transfer occurred 20 minutes earlier. The fund bought 11,198 ETH at an average price of $2,590 per ETH between February and March 2025 and currently has an unrealized loss of about $8.88 million.

data.title: Survey: 63% of Institutional Investors Say SEC Registration Could Bring Tokenized Assets Within Investment Mandates
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, a survey commissioned by ST0x and conducted by PureProfile in August 2026 found that 63% of 200 institutional investors and wealth management professionals said SEC registration could make tokenized assets eligible under their investment mandates. Another 48% said licensing the trading venue for an asset could help it meet those mandates.

Respondents represented investment managers, pension funds, insurers, family offices, banks, custodians and financial market infrastructure firms across North America, the UK, continental Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific. Asked what could increase trading volumes in tokenized securities, 29% cited automated corporate actions, 27% regulated custody and independent verification, and 19% legally enforceable rights to the underlying securities. Lower trading costs were cited by 3%.

data.title: Multiple U.S. Banks Hold Customers Liable for AI Agents’ Account Activity
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing TechCrunch, Citibank updated its online user agreement this week to say customers who authorize third-party AI agents to access their accounts are responsible for activity carried out by those agents. Customers are also liable for actions hackers take through their accounts if an AI tool exposes their credentials or is compromised. A Citibank spokesperson said the update clarifies the risks of sharing banking credentials or authorizing third-party tools to access accounts.

JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America announced similar policies last month, and PNC Bank revised its terms on November 18. Citizens Bank also emailed customers this week saying they are responsible for actions taken by AI assistants. Citibank’s agreement says customers do not assume additional liability when using the bank’s own AI agents.

data.title: Kernow Asset Management Bets on Beauty Tech Group’s Anti-Aging Demand
data.description: According to CNBC, Kernow Asset Management Chief Investment Officer Alyx Wood presented the hedge fund’s investment case for The Beauty Tech Group, a U.K.-listed maker of at-home beauty devices, at this year’s Sohn London investment conference. Wood sees the company as a way to invest in a broader shift toward beauty treatments that were once limited to clinics becoming smaller, cheaper and available for home use. He considers the company undervalued and sees substantial growth potential. The Beauty Tech Group reported pretax profit of £17.5 million in the first half of this year, more than triple the £5 million reported a year earlier. Wood’s valuation model put the shares at £15 ($19.70), compared with about £5 at the time of his presentation. Founded in 2009, the company went public in 2025, raising £29 million ($38.1 million). Its products include CurrentBody Skin, ZIIP Beauty and Tria Laser. Wood identified an upcoming dividend and broader eligibility for funds as potential catalysts, and said possible inclusion in the FTSE 250 was not far away.

data.title: China and U.S. Agree to Develop Plan for Constructive, Strategically Stable Relations
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Chinese President Xi Jinping met U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on November 19. The two sides agreed to develop an action plan for constructive, strategically stable relations, implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state, and build China-U.S. relations based on respect, fairness, and equality.

data.title: China Delays Soybean Imports at Ports as Domestic Stockpiles Build
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China is delaying the entry of soybean imports at some ports as weak demand from its vast livestock sector leaves domestic stockpiles overflowing.

data.title: AI | Hong Kong Family Office Unwinds $3.9 Billion in AI Bets
data.description: According to Bloomberg, the Hong Kong family office launched by hedge fund veteran Larry Chen unwound $3.9 billion in bets around AI and slashed its equity holdings last quarter, as investors broadly retreated from AI assets.

data.title: Alibaba Releases Qwen4-Max With 2.4 Trillion Parameters
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16. The model has 2.4 trillion total parameters, supports native vision and a 1 million-token context window, and activates 71 billion parameters per token. Alibaba said it ranked sixth on Code Arena and recorded results in Agents’ Last Exam, Vals Index, JobBench, and Chartography.

In Alibaba’s Work360 benchmark, Qwen4-Max outperformed its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max. In high-intensity reasoning mode, it used 35% fewer tokens and cut average task costs by about 60%. The model is available through QwenCloud’s Token Plan and API, as well as QwenWork and QwenStudio. Input costs $0.075 per 1 million tokens. Alibaba said smaller open-weight models in the Qwen4 series will be released to developers later.

data.title: €26 Million in Claims Await Verification as Dutch Bankrupt Crypto Exchange Knaken Registers 1,159 Creditors
data.description: Creditors of bankrupt Dutch crypto exchange Knaken have submitted claims totaling €26 million, which are awaiting verification. According to Odaily, a trustee’s latest report lists 1,159 registered creditors and says approximately €2.3 million has been recovered.

data.title: Jeff Bezos: Nvidia Should Look Internally for Its Next CEO
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos said Nvidia should look internally for its next CEO, arguing that an outside hire would have little chance of succeeding at a company with such a complex structure. He spoke on Tuesday at the “Silicon Valley and the World” event. Bezos, now co-CEO of AI engineering startup Prometheus, said he would not hire an outsider if Jensen Huang were not brought back, and that external recruitment should be a last resort.

Nvidia’s board has said it does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO. Harvey Jones, a longtime director appointed the company’s first chairman last week, said at the start of Tuesday afternoon’s earnings call that the board had “no intention” of restoring Huang to the role. The candidate pool will include internal and external candidates. The board wants to name a permanent CEO as soon as possible but will not rush its decision.

Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and CEO for 33 years, posted on X that morning that he was willing to return. He said he had made “serious mistakes” in his personal life and would cooperate with the board’s independent investigation. He wrote that he would be honored to return if the board determined it was in the best interests of shareholders, employees, the company and the United States. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who worked at Microsoft for 13 years, is serving as interim CEO.

Two major Nvidia investors, Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management, had urged the board to keep open the possibility of Huang’s return. Analyst Dan Ives said in a research note on Sunday that discussion of Huang returning was “unrealistic.” Bezos said Amazon’s CEO transition was not a suitable comparison: in 2021, he handed the role to longtime company executive Andy Jassy, whom he described as the architect of AWS, after extensive planning. Bezos said he did not know the details of Nvidia board discussions and could not judge whether Huang should return, but called him an outstanding founder worthy of admiration and respect. Bezos also said he would not take the role himself, adding that he enjoys running Prometheus.

data.title: Philippines Raises Over $450 Million in Retail Dollar Bond Comeback as Peso Rebounds
data.description: According to Bloomberg, the Philippines raised more than $450 million from retail dollar bonds on Thursday, returning to the market for such debt after three years as yields eased and the peso rebounded from a record low.

data.title: Alibaba Stock Falls 16.9% Ahead of Earnings as Chip Rule and AI Costs Weigh
data.description:
Alibaba shares fell 16.9% in five sessions to close Wednesday at $84.37, their lowest finish since January 2025, and were down 42% in 2026. A new U.S. chip rule, heavy AI spending and reduced share repurchases are pressuring the stock ahead of earnings, according to BeInCrypto. The Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule on Nov. 16 requiring licenses for advanced chips shipped to data centers serving China-headquartered companies at scale; commercial recommender systems are exempt, while data centers serving Chinese customers have 90 days, until mid-February 2027, to obtain a license. The rule takes effect on publication in the Federal Register, the same day results are due before the U.S. open on Thursday.

In the June quarter, capital expenditure rose 75% to RMB67.7 billion ($10 billion), while free cash flow was an outflow of RMB44.7 billion, compared with RMB18.8 billion a year earlier. Net income fell 75% to RMB10.4 billion and China e-commerce revenue declined 8%; cloud revenue grew 45%, with RMB5.6 billion in adjusted operating profit, while AI Labs and Applications lost RMB13.9 billion. Repurchases fell to $162 million in the June 2026 quarter from a peak of $5.8 billion in the June 2024 quarter. The program had $19.1 billion unused as of September 2025.

data.title: RBC Capital Markets Maintains Palo Alto Networks’ $475 Price Target, Citing AI-Driven Cybersecurity Demand
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, RBC Capital Markets reiterated its Outperform rating and $475 price target for Palo Alto Networks, saying cybersecurity threats associated with artificial intelligence will continue to drive security demand and that accelerating industry consolidation will create growth opportunities for the company.

The firm said Palo Alto Networks’ latest quarterly results broadly exceeded expectations, revenue growth accelerated, and all product lines performed strongly. Annual recurring revenue for its next-generation security business exceeded expectations by one of the widest margins in the company’s history. Palo Alto Networks also raised guidance for all major financial metrics for fiscal 2027, including its next-generation security annual recurring revenue outlook.

Palo Alto Networks announced plans to acquire Applied Compute for approximately $4.5 billion to enter the AI model-training field and offer customers secure open-weight models.

The company reported fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue of $3.44 billion, above market expectations of $3.31 billion. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.05, compared with expectations of $0.97.

data.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Shake Hands at APEC as Takaichi Is Kept at a Distance
data.description: According to CNBC, Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin met on the final day of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, where Trump held separate bilateral meetings with Xi and Putin. Trump and Putin shook hands during their first in-person talks in over a year. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spent several minutes trying to speak with Xi, who appeared not to respond, and no interpreter was present. International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said artificial intelligence and energy supply shocks had accelerated inflation in many economies and called for tighter monetary policy.

data.title: Investec Interim Profit Rises on Southern African Recovery
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Investec’s interim profit increased as a recovery in its southern African business offset a slowdown in its UK operations.

data.title: HSBC Launches Tokenized Hong Kong Dollar Money Market Fund With 100 RedCoin Minimum
data.description: HSBC said customers can use its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin (RCHKD), to subscribe to a new tokenized share class of the HSBC Global Money Market Fund – Hong Kong Dollar from November 19, with a minimum subscription of 100 RedCoin, equivalent to 100 Hong Kong dollars. According to Odaily, customers can trade the tokenized fund through HSBC Hong Kong and use RedCoin for subscription and settlement. RedCoin is issued under a license from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, can be exchanged for Hong Kong dollars at a 1:1 rate, and launched on October 23 through official channels including PayMe.

data.title: BNY: Preserving Fed Credibility May Require Excessive Monetary Tightening
data.description: According to Jin10, BNY Americas macro strategist John Velis said in a report that market expectations for policy rates continued to rise while inflation expectations barely changed, suggesting the Federal Reserve's credibility remained firm. He said markets still expected the Fed to take action against inflation, but the cost of preserving its credibility could be excessive monetary tightening. Interest-rate markets are now focused mainly on a possible Fed rate hike in December, while the policy path beyond December remains unclear.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Bret Taylor’s Sierra in Talks for Funding at a $30 Billion Valuation
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Sierra, the AI customer-service startup founded by Bret Taylor, former co-CEO of Salesforce, is discussing a new funding round targeting a valuation of about $30 billion. That would be nearly double the more than $15 billion valuation it announced in a previous round in May. One person familiar with the matter said the three-year-old startup is discussing raising about $1.5 billion. Lightspeed Venture Partners, Greenoaks and Benchmark are in talks to participate, though discussions are at an early stage and terms could change.

Sierra said last month that its annualized revenue had exceeded $400 million, double its level five months earlier. A company spokesperson declined to comment. The potential financing comes amid investor interest in AI application startups reporting rapid revenue growth.

Decagon, one of Sierra’s main competitors, had annualized revenue of about $100 million at the end of the second quarter and expects it to reach $175 million to $200 million by year-end, according to a person familiar with its executives. Decagon has also been discussing raising several hundred million dollars, but its target valuation is unknown.

Sierra has focused on large companies, including JPMorgan Chase, Cigna and Liberty Global, while Decagon has served startups and smaller businesses such as Perplexity, Notion and Duolingo. A person familiar with Decagon’s business said it recently added large customers including Delta, American Airlines, Hertz, Avis and Deutsche Telekom.

As companies try new AI tools, Sierra and Decagon have seen rapid revenue growth. However, many AI startups have gross margins below the 70%-plus level typical of traditional software companies. High costs for using leading AI models have weighed on margins, although model developers such as OpenAI have sharply reduced prices in recent months. Sierra and other AI application startups also employ technical consultants, sometimes called forward-deployed engineers, to help enterprise customers tailor the technology to specific use cases. Those labor costs can weigh on gross margins depending on how they are classified in accounting; Sierra’s gross margin is not known.

Sierra has previously raised more than $1.5 billion from investors including Tiger Global Management, GV, Greenoaks, Sequoia Capital and Benchmark.

data.title: AI | Wallenberg Investments Takes Minority Position in Swedish Firm Algoryx
data.description: The Wallenberg family’s investment vehicle has taken a minority stake in Swedish technology company Algoryx Simulation AB as it expands its work on artificial intelligence for autonomous machines, according to Bloomberg.
